evidence.excerpt:
Long-term memory remains a fundamental bottleneck for large language model
(LLM) agents across sessions. Existing systems typically adopt a write-then-
retrieve paradigm, storing context-dependent dialogue fragments and retrieving
them via nearest-neighbor search in continuous embedding space. This design
yields unstable access units and systematically misses logically related but lexi-
cally distant evidence. We propose MemCode, a long-term agent memory frame-
work that couples retrieval-oriented writing with discrete associative retrieval.
MemCode rewrites dialogue into self-contained atomic memory units (AMUs),
maps AMUs into a learnable codebook with isomorphic semantic quantization
(ISQ), and uses codebook co-occurrence topology as a retrieval path comple-
mentary to vector search. For long-term memory stores, MemCode separates on-
line atomic writes from asynchronous offline

RAG-style pipeline while adding a discrete representation layer
alongside continuous vectors, utilized throughout writing, retrieval, and long-term maintenance.
During writing, we employ LLM-based ingestion and abstraction to transform dialogue into self-
contained AMUs with source pointers. Each AMU serves as a minimal semantic unit that can be
independently retrieved. Independent semantic quantization (ISQ) anchors each AMU to a discrete
symbolic state within a learnable codebook. During retrieval, global codebook co-occurrence of-
fers an alternative access path for logically related yet geometrically distant memories, while source
pointers enhance context reconstruction. MemCode also separates online writing from offline con-
solidation, allowing clustering and synthesizing AMUs without disrupting real-time retrieval.

MemCode handles this with an asynchronous consolidation engine outside the online path. It back-
fills dense vectors, filters invalid entries, and applies hierarchical agglomerative clustering (HAC)
based on cosine distance [31]:

evidence.excerpt:
A Limitations
MemCode targets retrieval-intensive long-term conversational memory, not fully deployed agents
with planning, tool use, and interactive adaptation. Its LLM-based AMU writing can miss or distort
implicit motivations, emotions, and pragmatic cues; these cases explain why full-context methods
remain competitive on LoCoMo Open and bound our claims to structured memory retrieval. Our
HippoRAG2 comparison also measures one-shot graph construction over complete LoCoMo histo-
ries; repeated graph maintenance in a growing online memory is outside the present evaluation.

missing_information: No reproducible review or selection methodology was detected.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The codebook is frozen before memory evaluation, with no benchmark histories, questions, answers, labels, or retrieval traces entering its optimization; downstream accuracy is measured on disjoint benchmarks with ground-truth rubrics.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: End-to-end QA accuracy on LongMemEval-S and LoCoMo is scored by GPT-4o-mini as an LLM judge against ground-truth answers.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The discrete codebook is trained offline on DailyDialog context-response pairs using predictive cross-entropy and VQ commitment loss.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: The experimental claims are well-supported by the evidence: the codebook path specifically improves multi-hop and temporal recall without simply scaling candidate budgets, while limitations regarding open/affective questions and graph maintenance are honestly discussed.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluations on LongMemEval-S and LoCoMo against strong baselines (Mem0, LightMem, A-MEM, MemoryOS, HippoRAG2) with two LLM backbones show consistent improvements in accuracy alongside dramatic speedups in memory construction. Extensive controls (fixed budgets, BM25 replacement, dense embedding variations, repeated runs, and ablation studies) rigorously support the architectural hypotheses.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluation is carried out on downstream QA benchmark datasets completely disjoint from offline VQ codebook training, evaluated via standard benchmark rubrics and ground-truth comparisons across multiple runs and backbones.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: End-to-end question answering evaluated on LongMemEval-S and LoCoMo benchmarks using GPT-4o-mini as an LLM judge against ground-truth answers.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The discrete codebook component is trained offline using predictive cross-entropy and commitment loss on DailyDialog context-response pairs.

primary.limitations: The authors clearly acknowledge the boundary conditions of AMU abstraction, noting that implicit emotional or pragmatic cues can be lost compared to full-context baselines, and that the evaluation focuses on conversational memory retrieval rather than agentic planning or dynamic multi-step graph updates.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing atomic memory unit (AMU) generation with source pointers, stride-1 VQ-VAE discrete semantic quantization on DailyDialog, graph-like co-occurrence retrieval with IDF discounting, and offline HAC-based consolidation.
primary.quality_rationale: The paper provides an innovative, technically sound, and well-executed architecture for agent memory retrieval that addresses geometric limitations of purely dense representations. Experimental methodology is thorough and well-controlled with extensive ablations.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces MemCode, a long-term agent memory framework combining atomic memory extraction with isomorphic semantic quantization (VQ-VAE codebook learning) for dual-path (dense vector and discrete topology co-occurrence) retrieval and asynchronous consolidation.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The paper provides an innovative, technically sound, and well-executed architecture for agent memory retrieval that addresses geometric limitations of purely dense representations. Experimental methodology is thorough and well-controlled with extensive ablations.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors clearly acknowledge the boundary conditions of AMU abstraction, noting that implicit emotional or pragmatic cues can be lost compared to full-context baselines, and that the evaluation focuses on conversational memory retrieval rather than agentic planning or dynamic multi-step graph updates.
